_about: Starter culture items. Each one's rights come from the holder's own record (Cleveland Museum of Art open access API, The Met collection API, Project Gutenberg), checked on the date given. Descriptions are ours, from the holder's catalogue.

items.title: A Norfolk Plough (Liber Studiorum, plate 43)
items.creator: John Sell Cotman (British, 1782–1842)
items.description: A soft-ground etching of a plough in Norfolk, from a volume of 48 plates.
items.licence: CC0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
items.credit: John Sell Cotman, A Norfolk Plough, 1814. The Cleveland Museum of Art, CC0.

items.title: Haymakers
items.creator: Thomas Rowlandson (British, 1757–1827)
items.description: An etching and aquatint of haymakers by the caricaturist Thomas Rowlandson.
items.licence: Public domain (The Met Open Access, CC0)
items.credit: Thomas Rowlandson, Haymakers, 1787. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, public domain.

items.title: Harvest Scene
items.creator: Anonymous, British
items.description: A hand-coloured mezzotint of a harvest, by an unknown British printmaker.
items.licence: Public domain (The Met Open Access, CC0)
items.credit: Anonymous British printmaker, Harvest Scene, 18th century. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, public domain.

items.title: Rowing Home the Schoof-Stuff
items.creator: Peter Henry Emerson (British, 1856–1936)
items.description: A photograph from Emerson's book Life and Landscape on the Norfolk Broads (1886). The museum notes he set out to photograph rural life directly, against the sentimental pictures of his day.
items.licence: CC0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
items.credit: Peter Henry Emerson, Rowing Home the Schoof-Stuff, 1886. The Cleveland Museum of Art, CC0.

items.title: End of the Harvest
items.creator: Charles Angrand (French, 1854–1926)
items.description: A charcoal drawing of the end of a harvest, by a French artist associated with Pointillism.
items.licence: CC0 (Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access)
items.credit: Charles Angrand, End of the Harvest, c. 1892–1905. The Cleveland Museum of Art, CC0.

items.title: He that would thrive
items.creator: Traditional, collected by J. O. Halliwell
items.made_text: Traditional; in The Nursery Rhymes of England (fifth edition, 1886)
items.description: A traditional rhyme about rising early and working the plough.
items.credit: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell, fifth edition (London: Frederick Warne, 1886), no. XCIII.

items.title: In July, some reap rye
items.creator: Traditional, collected by J. O. Halliwell
items.made_text: Traditional; in The Nursery Rhymes of England (fifth edition, 1886)
items.description: A traditional rhyme about the harvest months.
items.text:
In July,
Some reap rye;
In August,
If one will not the other must.
items.credit: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell, fifth edition (London: Frederick Warne, 1886), no. CIII.

items.title: I was an innkeeper (from an alphabet rhyme)
items.creator: Traditional, collected by J. O. Halliwell
items.made_text: Traditional; in The Nursery Rhymes of England (fifth edition, 1886)
items.description: Lines from an alphabet rhyme naming trades, including a farmer and an innkeeper.
items.text:
F was a farmer, and followed the plough.
…
I was an innkeeper, who lov'd to bouse,
J was a joiner, and built up a house.
items.credit: The Nursery Rhymes of England, collected by J. O. Halliwell, fifth edition (London: Frederick Warne, 1886).
